McDonnell Douglas F-15E Strike Eagle: United States. The McDonnell Douglas (now Boeing) F-15E Strike Eagle is an American all-weather multirole strike fighter derived from the McDonnell Douglas F-15 Eagle.
Who is credited with discovering Nihonium?
Nihonium: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research. Nihonium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Nh and atomic number 113.
Who is credited with discovering Mass–energy equivalence?
Mass–energy equivalence: Albert Einstein. In physics, mass–energy equivalence is the relationship between mass and energy in a system's rest frame.
Who is credited with discovering Plesiosaurus?
Plesiosaurus: Mary Anning. It is known by nearly complete skeletons from the Lias of England.
First nominated by Ronald Reagan in 1987 and reappointed every four years until 2006, this economist ran the Federal Reserve for its second-longest tenure ever — who is he?
Alan Greenspan (born March 6, 1926) is an American economist who served as the 13th chairman of the Federal Reserve from 1987 to 2006.
This English number theorist became a mathematical legend by proving Fermat's Last Theorem, earning the 2016 Abel Prize and a knighthood. Who is he?
Andrew Wiles (born 11 April 1953) is an English mathematician and a Royal Society Research Professor at the University of Oxford, specialising in number theory.

A German former computer repair technician, this man received international attention after murdering and cannibalizing a voluntary victim he had found over the Internet in March 2001, and was ultimately convicted of murder in a 2006 retrial — who is he?

Armin Meiwes (born 1 December 1961) is a German former computer repair technician who received international attention for murdering and cannibalising Bernd Brandes, whom he had found via the Internet as a voluntary victim, in March 2001.
The second-largest living rodents after capybaras, these large semiaquatic mammals of the Northern Hemisphere have webbed back feet, hand-like front paws, and flat, scaly tails — name the animal?
Beaver (genus Castor) are large semiaquatic rodents of the Northern Hemisphere.

Believed to descend from hounds kept at a Belgian abbey and used by police worldwide to track escaped prisoners, this scent hound can discern a person's trail days after they've passed — name this dog breed?
Bloodhound is a large scent hound, originally bred for hunting deer, wild boar, rabbits, and since the Middle Ages, for tracking people.
This condition results from inflamed, fluid-filled sacs that cushion friction points between bones, tendons, and muscles, commonly striking the shoulder, elbow, hip, or knee — what is it?
Bursitis is the inflammation of one or more bursae in the body.
This large, stocky black corvid fills a niche across Eurasia comparable to a similar bird found in North America, but is bigger and huskier than its transatlantic counterpart — what species is it?
Carrion crow (Corvus corone) is a passerine bird of the family Corvidae, native to western Europe and the eastern Palearctic.
Besides identifying the laws of elastic collision, this Dutch polymath studied Saturn's rings and improved the design of the telescope — who is he?
Christiaan Huygens (14 April 1629 - 8 July 1695) was a Dutch mathematician, physicist, engineer, astronomer, and inventor who is regarded as a key figure in the Scientific Revolution.
This activity involves designing algorithms and writing code in high-level languages so a machine can follow step-by-step instructions to perform tasks. What is it?
Computer programming is the composition of sequences of instructions, called programs, that computers can follow to perform tasks.
This Zambian-born economist turned four of her five books into New York Times bestsellers, including a provocative argument that foreign aid actually holds Africa back — who is she?
Dambisa Moyo, Baroness Moyo (born 2 February 1969) is a Zambian-born economist and author, known for her analysis of macroeconomics and global affairs.
Made from a fermented batter of ground black gram and rice, this thin South Indian bread is traditionally served with chutney and sambar — what is it?

Dosa (food) (in Indian English) or thosai (in Malaysian English and Singapore English) is a thin, savoury batter bread in South Indian cuisine made from a fermented batter of ground black gram and rice.

These ductless glands throughout the body secrete their products directly into the bloodstream rather than through a duct — together with the pineal, pituitary, thyroid, and others, what are they called?
Endocrine gland is a network of glands and organs located throughout the body.
This Chinese-born American computer scientist built ImageNet, the dataset that supercharged computer vision in the 2010s, and co-directs Stanford's Human-Centered AI institute — who is she?

Fei-Fei Li (pinyin: L Fifi; born July 3, 1976) is a Chinese-born American computer scientist best known for establishing ImageNet, the dataset that enabled rapid advances in computer vision in the 2010s.

Found from the tropics to subarctic regions and accounting for about 88% of living amphibian species, this tailless, semiaquatic creature has a name that informally splits into 'toad' for the warty ones — what is it?
Frog is any member of a diverse and largely semiaquatic group of short-bodied, tailless amphibian vertebrates composing the order Anura (coming from the Ancient Greek, literally 'without tail').
One of the most widely distributed eagles in the Northern Hemisphere, this raptor is dark brown with lighter plumage on its nape and white markings on immature birds — which bird of prey?
Golden eagle (Aquila chrysaetos) is a bird of prey living in the Northern Hemisphere.

This now-outdated astronomical model placed the Sun rather than the Earth at the center of the universe, eventually replacing the geocentric view before itself being superseded by relativity — what model is it?
Heliocentrism (also known as the heliocentric model) is a superseded astronomical model that placed the Sun at the center of the universe, with the Earth and the planets in its orbit.

Also called prussic acid, this highly toxic and flammable liquid boils just above room temperature at 25.6 degrees Celsius. It is produced industrially as a precursor to many chemical compounds, particularly potassium cyanide and adiponitrile. What is it?
Hydrogen cyanide (also called prussic acid) is a chemical compound with the formula HCN and structural formula HCN.
Founder of Romania's Social Democratic Party, this engineer served two separate stints as president after playing a leading role in the 1989 revolution that toppled Ceaușescu — who is he?

Ion Iliescu (3 March 1930 - 5 August 2025) was a Romanian politician and engineer who served as the first and third President of Romania since the country's transition to democracy, from 1990 to 1996 and 2000 to 2004.
Originally trained as a mathematician, this English economist built the foundation for an entire school of macroeconomic thought that bears his name — who is he?

John Maynard Keynes (KAYNZ; 5 June 1883 - 21 April 1946), was an English economist whose writings are considered the basis for the school of thought known as Keynesian economics, as well as its various offshoots.
When the natural curve of the thoracic spine exceeds about 45 degrees, doctors give this excessive rounding of the upper back a name rooted in the Greek word for 'hump' — what is it?
Kyphosis (from Greek (kyphos) 'hump') is an abnormally excessive convex curvature of the spine as it occurs in the thoracic and sacral regions.
Serving as a somatosensory organ as well as a tool for eating and forming sounds, this pair of soft facial features is one of the most visible parts of the mouth — what are they?
Lip are a horizontal pair of soft appendages attached to the jaws and are the most visible part of the mouth of many animals, including humans.
Roughly 60% the diameter of Pluto and stained reddish-brown by tholins, this trans-Neptunian dwarf planet carries minor-planet number 136472 — what is it?
Makemake (minor-planet number 136472) is a dwarf planet orbiting the Sun in the Kuiper belt, a disc of icy bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune.
This genus of about 20 species in the Lamiaceae family readily hybridizes where different species' ranges overlap, and thrives best in wet, moist soils — what genus is it?
Mentha (from Greek mntha, Linear B mi-ta), is a genus of flowering plants in the mint family, Lamiaceae.

Native to Africa, Asia, and Oceania, with one invasive species now in the southern U.S., this reptile genus ranges from 20 centimeters long to over 3 meters in the Komodo dragon — name this group of lizards?
Monitor lizard are lizards in the genus Varanus, the only extant genus in the family Varanidae.

Discovered in 1898 alongside krypton and xenon, this colorless noble gas is famous for the distinctive bright-red glow it emits, which led to its immediate identification as a new element — what gas, symbol Ne, is it?
Neon is a chemical element; it has the symbol Ne and the atomic number 10.

This branch of medicine focuses on the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of cancer, a disease first documented in Egypt as early as 3000 BCE in the Edwin Smith papyrus — what is this medical specialty called?
Oncology is a branch of medicine that deals with the study, treatment, diagnosis, and prevention of cancer.
Named after a 17th-century French mathematician and physicist, this SI unit of pressure is defined as one newton of force per square metre — name the unit?
Pascal (unit) (symbol: Pa) is the unit of pressure in the International System of Units (SI).
Ranging in color from clear to yellow, green, or even grey, this respiratory mucus is expelled through coughing and also goes by the name sputum — what is it?
Phlegm (Ancient) is mucus produced by the respiratory system, excluding that produced by the throat and nose passages.
Ranging from linear chains to heavily branched polymers, these carbohydrate compounds — like starch, glycogen, and chitin — consist of many simple sugar units linked together. What are they called?
Polysaccharide (from Ancient Greek (pols) 'many, much' and (skkhar) 'sugar') are "compounds consisting of a large number of monosaccharides linked glycosidically".
Nesting in burrows or rock crevices on coastal cliffs, this black-and-white seabird can dive underwater to feed and beats its short wings up to 400 times per minute in flight — what bird is it?
Puffin are any of three species of small alcids (auks) in the bird genus Fratercula.
Which large Southern African dog breed, whose standard was drafted in 1922 in what's now Zimbabwe, descends from ridged hunting dogs of the Khoikhoi crossed with European breeds used to bay lions?
Rhodesian Ridgeback is a large dog breed originally bred in Southern Africa.
Once placed in its own plant family before molecular studies folded it into Dracaena, this African and Asian succulent genus includes the plant nicknamed 'devil's tongue' — which genus?

Sansevieria is a historically recognized genus of flowering plants, native to Africa, notably Madagascar, and southern Asia, now included in the genus Dracaena on the basis of molecular phylogenetic studies.
Named for its enormous shoe-shaped bill, this grey wading bird of East African swamps was once filed with storks but now sits beside pelicans — and its closest kin is the hamerkop — what is it?
Shoebill (Balaeniceps rex), also known as the whale-headed stork, whalebill, and shoe-billed stork, is a large long-legged wading bird.

This class of moisture-loving hexapods — the largest lineage of six-legged creatures excluded from the insect group — indirectly aids decomposition by breaking down organic matter and shaping soil microbial life. What are they?
Springtail (class Collembola) form the largest of the three lineages of modern hexapods that are no longer considered insects, the others being Protura and Diplura.
Serving as prime minister seven separate times before becoming president from 1993 to 2000, this Turkish statesman led two different political parties across his long career — who was he?
Süleyman Demirel (1 November 1924 - 17 June 2015) was a Turkish politician, engineer, and statesman who served as the president of Turkey from 1993 to 2000.
This herb is also called common thyme or garden thyme and belongs to the mint family, Lamiaceae — which species is it?
Thymus vulgaris (common thyme, German thyme, garden thyme or just thyme) is a species of flowering plant in the mint family, Lamiaceae.
This break in the skin or mucous membrane involves tissue breakdown severe enough to expose the dermis or fat beneath, and often becomes infected with pus — what condition is it?
Ulcer (dermatology) is a sore on the skin or a mucous membrane, accompanied by the disintegration of tissue.
This unit of time, equal to seven days, serves as the standard calendrical period between a day and a month in most of the world. What is it?
Week (in the Western and international context) is a unit of time equal to seven days.
Also called motor neuron disease or Lou Gehrig's disease, this terminal condition progressively destroys the neurons that control voluntary muscle movement — what is it?
Nicknamed the painted hunter for its mottled coat, this sub-Saharan canine hunts cooperatively at dawn and dusk and is the only living member of its genus, Lycaon — which species?
African wild dog: Species of canine. The African wild dog (Lycaon pictus), also called painted dog and Cape hunting dog, is a wild canine native to sub-Saharan Africa.
Unlike its bulb-forming relative, the common onion, this perennial vegetable never forms a bulb and owes one of its names to its hollow, tube-like leaves — which plant?
Allium fistulosum: Species of plant. The species is very similar in taste and odor to the related common onion, Allium cepa, and hybrids between the two (tree onions) exist.
A branch of morphology with roots in prehistoric times, which natural science studies the internal and external structure of organisms and their parts?
Anatomy: Study of the structure of organisms. Anatomy is a branch of natural science that deals with the structural organization of living things.
Also known as Umbelliferae and including carrots, celery, parsley, and dill, this plant family also contains dangerously toxic members like poison hemlock and giant hogweed — which family?

One of its founders, James Keeler, said this science 'seeks to ascertain the nature of the heavenly bodies... rather than their positions or motions' — studying everything from the Sun to the cosmic microwave background. What field is it?
A tender herb of the mint family native from Central Africa to Southeast Asia, its Genovese or 'sweet' variety is a kitchen staple worldwide — what is it?
Basil: Culinary herb. Basil (Ocimum basilicum), also called great basil, is a culinary herb of the family Lamiaceae (mints).

Closely related to the beech-oak family and including species widespread across the Northern Hemisphere's temperate and boreal zones, which thin-leaved deciduous hardwood genus is prized for its versatile wood?
Birch: Genus of flowering plants in the family Betulaceae.
This highly venomous snake in the Colubridae family, scientifically known as Dispholidus typus, is native to Sub-Saharan Africa — what is its common name?
One of the largest snake species on Earth, this Southeast Asian native became invasive in Florida after escaping the pet trade — which snake is this?
Burmese python: Species of large, nonvenomous snake.
Produced by chili peppers likely to deter hungry mammals, this hydrophobic compound is what gives them their burning, pungent kick — what is it?
Capsaicin: Pungent chemical compound in chili peppers. It is a potent irritant for mammals for which it produces a sensation of burning in any tissue with which it comes into contact.

This biological process splits a parent into two daughters, either producing genetically identical copies via mitosis or reducing chromosome number by half via meiosis to form gametes. What process is it?
Cell division: Biological process. Cell division usually occurs as part of a larger cell cycle in which the cell grows and replicates its chromosome(s) before dividing.

This antibiotic is used as an eye ointment for conjunctivitis and, when safer options fail, to treat meningitis, plague, cholera, and typhoid — but in newborns it can trigger a dangerous swelling condition called gray baby syndrome — what drug is it?
Chloramphenicol: Antibiotic. Chloramphenicol is an antibiotic useful for the treatment of a number of bacterial infections.
This French inventor born near Toulouse is remembered chiefly as an aviation pioneer, but in 1870 he was also among the first to take up the sport of cycling in France — who is it?
Clément Ader: French inventor and engineer (1841–1925)
Better known as "pink eye," this inflammation of the clear layer over the white of the eye can leave a lid stuck shut by morning — what's the medical name?

Conjunctivitis: Inflammation of the eye. Conjunctivitis, also known as pink eye, is inflammation of the conjunctiva, the thin and clear layer that covers the white surface of the eye and the inner eyelid.
This species includes honeydew, cantaloupe, and Casaba varieties, and traveled along ancient caravan routes long before its exact origin in the Levant or Egypt was ever confirmed — what fruit is it?
Cucumis melo: Species of plant. Cucumis melo, also known as melon or true melon, is a species of Cucumis that has been developed into many cultivated varieties.
Native to Madagascar and grown ornamentally throughout the tropics, this legume tree is known for its fern-like leaves and a flamboyant summer display of orange-red blossoms — what is it?
Delonix regia: Species of flowering plant in the bean family Fabaceae.
Also nicknamed the French Mastiff, this large, powerfully muscled brachycephalic breed ranks among France's heaviest dogs — which breed?
Dogue de Bordeaux: Dog breed originating in France.
This American astronomer proved that many so-called nebulae were actually separate galaxies, and in 1929 showed that galaxies recede faster the farther away they are — who is he?
Triggered by the parasympathetic nervous system and a rise in nitric oxide, this physiological event leaves an organ firm and engorged — what is it?
Erection: Physiological phenomenon involving the hardening and enlargement of the penis.

Also known as the wisent, this species is the heaviest wild land mammal on its continent — hunted to extinction in the wild by the early 20th century before being restored through captive breeding programs. Which animal?
European bison: Eurasian species of mammal. It is one of two extant species of bison, alongside the American bison.
This genus of about 850 tropical tree, shrub, and vine species is best known for two cultivated fruit-bearing members and serves as a vital food source for wildlife across the tropics — which genus?
Ficus: Genus of flowering plants in the mulberry family Moraceae.
Before becoming Ferrari's Formula One team principal in 2023, this Frenchman co-founded a junior-racing outfit that won back-to-back titles with Lewis Hamilton and Nico Rosberg — who is he?
Combining Greek words for 'earth,' 'form,' and 'study,' what field examines how landscapes and seafloor features form and evolve over time?
This common name covers edible fruit from the Ribes genus — the same genus as currants — coming in colors from green and red to purple, yellow, white, or black — which fruit?
Gooseberry: Species of Ribes cultivated for its edible fruit.
Producing up to a hundred billion new cells a day from specialized stem cells, this biological process manufactures every component of blood — what is it?
Haematopoiesis: Formation of blood cellular components.
Introduced to Britain in the 19th century as an ornamental plant, this Caucasus-native's sap causes painful blistering burns when exposed skin meets sunlight — which species?
Heracleum mantegazzianum: Species of flowering plant. Heracleum mantegazzianum, commonly known as giant hogweed, is a monocarpic perennial herbaceous plant in the carrot family Apiaceae.

In the Renaissance this field of study covered classical literature and language rather than religion or divinity, and today it groups subjects using critical and interpretive methods rather than empirical ones — what broad academic category is this?
Humanities: Academic disciplines that study society and culture.
This Russian-American engineer built the first successful four-engine aircraft in 1913 and went on to pioneer the modern helicopter — who was he?
Nicknamed 'Dr. Death,' this pathologist assisted at least 130 patients in dying and was convicted of murder after broadcasting one such case on television — who is he?
Jack Kevorkian: American pathologist and euthanasia activist (1928–2011)
This physician ran the Battle Creek Sanitarium — part spa, part hospital, part luxury hotel — where he treated the rich and poor alike and devised numerous nut and vegetable products — who is it?
This German-Finnish internet entrepreneur founded the file-hosting service Megaupload before U.S. authorities seized it in 2012 — who is he?
This biennial vegetable in the onion family has an edible bundle of leaf sheaths sometimes colloquially called a 'stem' — what is it?
Leek: Vegetable in the onion family. A leek is a biennial vegetable, a cultivar of Allium ampeloprasum, the broadleaf wild leek (syn.
Named after both a biblical sea monster and the author of 'Moby-Dick,' this extinct predatory sperm whale roamed ancient oceans roughly 9 million years ago — which genus?
Livyatan: Extinct genus of sperm whale from the Miocene epoch.
Native to northeastern Australia and first commercially grown at scale in Hawaii during the 1880s, this is the only widely cultivated food plant indigenous to Australia — what nut is it?
Macadamia: Genus of plants indigenous to Australia.
Kangaroos, koalas, and wombats all belong to this mammal group whose young are born undeveloped and finish developing in their mother's pouch — what group is it?
Marsupial: Infraclass of mammals in the clade Metatheria.
Cataloged as a nebula by a French astronomer in 1781, this supergiant elliptical galaxy boasts roughly 15,000 globular clusters, a hundred times more than our own — which galaxy is it?
Messier 87: Galaxy in the constellation Virgo.
This industry extracts everything from coal and gemstones to rock salt and gravel from the Earth, but is also linked to land degradation and habitat loss — what is it?
Mining: Extraction of valuable minerals or other geological materials from the Earth.
In this autoimmune disease the immune system attacks myelin, the insulation around nerve cells, so the central nervous system can't transmit signals properly — what condition?
Multiple sclerosis: Disease that damages the myelin sheaths around nerves.
Commonly called horsehair worms, these parasitoid animals get their nickname from the Gordian knot because of how they tangle themselves up — what phylum is this?

Nematomorpha: Phylum of parasitoid animals; horsehair worms. The adult worms are free-living, but the larvae are parasitic on arthropods, such as beetles, cockroaches, mantises, orthopterans, and crustaceans.
This Turkish-born American economist, a Harvard-trained NYU professor, earned lasting fame as one of the few who foresaw the 2008 subprime mortgage crisis. Who is he?
With atomic number 76 and symbol Os, this bluish-white transition metal has the highest density of any stable element and was once prized for fountain-pen nib tips — what is it?
Osmium: Chemical element with atomic number 76 (Os). Osmium (from Ancient Greek ὀσμή (osmḗ) 'smell') is a chemical element; it has symbol Os and atomic number 76.

First described by a 17th-century French mathematician in 1653, this fluid mechanics principle states that a pressure change at any point in a confined, incompressible fluid is felt equally throughout it — what's it called?
Pascal's law: Principle in fluid mechanics. The law was established by French mathematician Blaise Pascal in 1653 and published in 1663.
Named from a Tupi-Guarani word for tobacco filtered through French, this South American flowering plant genus is a garden hybrid favorite — which plant?
Petunia: Genus of flowering plants. The popular flower of the same name derived its epithet from the French, which took the word pétun, 'tobacco', from a Tupi–Guarani language.

A member of the cashew family, this tree nut is a priority allergen, yet the world still churned out 1.4 million tonnes in 2024 — with the US, Iran, and Turkey making up 87% of it. Which green-hued nut is it?
Pistachio: Member of the cashew family. The pistachio (UK also; Pistacia vera) is a small to medium-sized tree of the cashew family.
This imperial unit of pressure equals about 6.895 kilopascals and is the number you check when filling a bicycle tire to around 65 — which unit?
Pound per square inch: Unit of pressure or stress. It is the pressure resulting from a force with magnitude of one pound-force applied to an area of one square inch.

Covering the asymmetric relationship between citizens and the state — including constitutional, administrative, tax, and criminal matters — this branch of the legal system contrasts with the branch governing relationships between individuals — which branch?
Public law: Law governing government actions.
One of the oldest groups of eukaryotic seaweed, this phylum boasts over 7,000 species — mostly marine, though about 5% live in freshwater habitats. What group is it?
Red algae: Division of plant life.

Also called black locust or false acacia, this deciduous legume-family tree is native to just a few small pockets of the United States but has been planted so widely it's now considered invasive elsewhere — which tree?
Robinia pseudoacacia: Species of tree native to North America.
Native to Mexico and Guatemala, this mint-family plant is prized for its hydrophilic seeds known as chia — what's its scientific name?
Salvia hispanica: Species of flowering plant in the mint family.
Encompassing several superfamilies and families, this taxonomic order groups together cephalopods that each have ten arms — which order is it?
Found from Bangladesh to the Philippines, these nocturnal primates make up the genus Nycticebus and include at least eight recognized species — what are they called?
Slow loris: Genus of primates from Southeast Asia.
The sole living member of its genus, this slender, long-legged antelope of southwest Africa sports a white face, a dark eye-to-mouth stripe, and backward-curving horns on both sexes — what is it?
Springbok: Antelope of southwest and south Africa. The springbok or springbuck (Antidorcas marsupialis) is an antelope found mainly in south and southwest Africa.
Described as the most economically important oxide of its element, this compound with the formula SO3 is a key precursor to sulfuric acid and to acid rain — what is it?
Sulfur trioxide: Chemical compound. Sulfur trioxide exists in several forms: gaseous monomer, crystalline trimer, and solid polymer.
Which calculus result approximates a differentiable function near a point using a polynomial — its first-order version being the familiar linear approximation?

Taylor's theorem: Approximation of a function by a polynomial. There are several versions of Taylor's theorem, some giving explicit estimates of the approximation error of the function by its Taylor polynomial.
Commonly nicknamed 'tree of life' from Latin, this genus of coniferous evergreens in the cypress family includes species native to both North America and eastern Asia. What's the genus?
Thuja: Genus of conifers. Thuja ( THEW-yə) is a genus of coniferous tree or shrub in the Cupressaceae (cypress family).
Which mathematical principle states that, for any three-sided shape, the sum of two side lengths must be at least as long as the third?
Triangle inequality: Property of geometry, also used to generalize the notion of "distance" in metric spaces.
This hormone-responsive organ nourishes a developing embryo and fetus until birth, connecting at its narrow lower end to the cervix and at its upper corners to the fallopian tubes — what is it?
Uterus: Female sex organ in mammals.
Also called Japanese horseradish, this pungent rhizome is ground into a paste for sushi and has been recorded as a food since the 8th century — what is it?
Known as the 'grunting ox,' this long-haired domesticated bovine roams the Tibetan Plateau and Himalayan region, descended from a wild ancestor called Bos mutus — what animal is it?
The symbol for silver is Ag. Silver is a chemical element; it has symbol Ag and atomic number 47.
The symbol for mercury is Hg.

Cher (SHAIR; legally mononymous; born Cheryl Sarkisian, May 20, 1946) is an American singer and actress.

Olga Kurylenko: Olga Kostyantynivna Kurylenko (born 14 November 1979) is a Ukrainian-born French actress and former model.
In what year was Gal Gadot born?
Gal Gadot (Hebrew: גל גדות, pronounced [ˈɡal ɡaˈdot]; born 30 April 1985) is an Israeli actress.
In what year was Lily-Rose Depp born?
Lily-Rose Depp: Lily-Rose Melody Depp (born May 27, 1999) is a French and American actress and singer.
In what year was Fran Drescher born?
Fran Drescher: Francine Joy Drescher (born September 30, 1957) is an American actress, writer, comedian, producer, and former trade union leader.

Chuck Norris: Carlos Ray "Chuck" Norris (March 10, 1940 – March 19, 2026) was an American martial artist, actor, screenwriter, and author.

Prabhas made his acting debut with the drama Eeswar (2002) and later attained his breakthrough with the action romance Varsham (2004).
In what year was George Lucas born?
George Lucas: George Walton Lucas Jr. (born May 14, 1944) is an American filmmaker and philanthropist.

Golshifteh Farahani: Rahavard Farahani (Persian: رهاورد فراهانی; born 10 July 1983), known professionally as Golshifteh Farahani (گلشیفته فراهانی), is an Iranian actress.
In what year was Robert Redford born?
Robert Redford: Redford began his career on television in the late 1950s, appearing in anthology series such as Alfred Hitchcock Presents and The Twilight Zone.
In what year was James Caan born?
James Caan: James Edmund Caan ( KAHN; March 26, 1940 – July 6, 2022) was an American actor.
In what year did Roald Dahl die?
Roald Dahl: Dahl was born in Wales to affluent Norwegian immigrant parents, and lived for most of his life in England.
In what year was Dr. No first released?
Dr. No (film): No is a 1962 spy film and the first film in the James Bond series, starring Sean Connery as the fictional MI6 agent James Bond.
In what year was Asteroid City first released?
Asteroid City: The play is contexualised through a television documentary following the creation of the show itself, adding a layer of metatextuality.
In what year was Civil War first released?
Civil War (film): With a budget of $50 million, Civil War was A24's most expensive film at the time.
In what year was Dumb Money first released?
Dumb Money is a 2023 American biographical comedy-drama film, directed by Craig Gillespie and written by Lauren Schuker Blum and Rebecca Angelo.
